mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat during the high-rate period, with a p-value > 0.05 in a two-sample test against the pre-rate hike period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coincides with stronger consumer demand (GDPC1) and reduces labor market tightness, weakening corporate profit expectations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate exceeds 100,000 jobs/month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during similar labor growth expansions.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the market anticipates a faster than expected Fed response, causing a sharp decline in equity valuations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and remain so for at least 10 consecutive 5-day windows during high inflation periods.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 90 for two months signals supply-side weakness that reduces future earnings growth assumptions, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: INDPRO remains below 90 for more than 6 months without a corresponding S&P 500 upward surprise in forward returns.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in UNRATE turns positive for the first time in three months, it indicates a shift toward tighter labor market conditions, prompting higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the first 3 months of UNRATE decline before the rate hike signal.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising job openings (PAYEMS) without a corresponding rise in unemployment (implied by UNRATE) suggest a strong labor market, which can suppress equity valuations through higher risk premiums, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases for two consecutive months while UNRATE remains below 5%
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are non-negative and statistically insignificant (p > 0.10) during similar labor cycles.
